anomalies.observed: Both UART3 connector signal lines are tied to FCC1 pins that are VCAP (internal regulator decoupling output, power_out type), not to a GPIO or USART pin. UART3_RX_FCC is on pin 73 and UART3_TX_FCC on pin 48. Both VCAP pins are also absent from the FCC1 pin list used elsewhere, so the UART3 connector is wired onto the MCU's internal core-supply pins.
anomalies.expected: UART3 TX/RX should connect to USART pins of the STM32H753 (alternate-function GPIO). The VCAP pins should only connect to their decoupling capacitor and must not drive or receive signals.
anomalies.impact: The UART3 connector cannot communicate with the FCC MCU. The VCAP pins are driven by the internal 1.2 V core regulator and are loaded by the connector, which can destabilise the core supply and cause the FCC to malfunction or fail to boot.

anomalies.observed: Decoupling capacitor C13 (2u2, 0603) has pad 1 unconnected. Its only connection is pad 2 to GND, so it does nothing.
anomalies.expected: A decoupling capacitor on the FCC supply should connect between a supply rail and GND.
anomalies.impact: Minor. The capacitor provides no decoupling, and the FCC supply has one less bypass capacitor than intended.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address-select pin A0 (U2.1) is tied to the 3.3 V supply rather than GND, while A1 to A5 are tied to GND. The resulting address is 0x41, not 0x40. The INA219 (U1) on the same I2C2_SCL_FCC/I2C2_SDA_FCC bus is at 0x40 (A0 and A1 to GND).
anomalies.expected: The specification gives the PCA9685PW I2C address as 0x40, which requires A0 to be tied to GND (all address pins low).
anomalies.impact: The firmware addressing the PWM driver at 0x40 will get no response, so the servo outputs will not be driven. If A0 is changed to 0x40 the PWM driver would collide with the INA219 on the same bus.

parsed.summary: The most likely anomaly is the FCC UART3 connector lines wired onto the STM32H753's VCAP core-supply pins, which is a bridged-net error that would break UART3 and load the internal regulator. Two lower-confidence items are a floating decoupling capacitor and a PCA9685 address strap that conflicts with the specification.
